newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus says restructuring talks continue.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says restructuring talks continue.

text.p: Talks on changing European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie into an integrated company from the present partnership structure are continuing, a spokesman for the group said on Monday.

Airbus has said Sunday's merger announcement between its U.S. rivals Boeing and McDonnell Douglas would not change the commercial challenge as Douglas has been a diminishing force in the civilian aircraft market.
The four Airbus partners said on July 8 they aimed to reach a binding agreement by the end of 1996 on the timetable for forming the new Airbus company, which could be formed by 1999.
"The discussions go on. The partners are still working on negotiations for the Airbus Industrie restructuring," he said.
Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
The Airbus board held its routine monthly meeting on Friday, said the spokesman, who gave no details of the restructuring talks.

The Boeing-MD merger, if approved by the U.S. authorities, would create the world's biggest aerospace company with annual sales of $48 billion and employ 200,000 employees. The merger is valued at $13.3 billion with a stock swap.
Industry sources said there are three distinct positions held by the Airbus partners over the shape of the new Airbus, which is needed to boost competitiveness.
Aerospatiale's chairman Yves Michot said in September he wants an Airbus acting as a prime contractor with enlarged project management powers to direct the work of subcontractors.
That "minimalist" Airbus would essentially maintain the current functions but add elements such as full product support.
Dasa wants a "maximalist" Airbus, which would integrate the manufacturing, design and engineering of major systems but also the work on subsystems.
BAe favours retaining the "core assets" withing the new company, including the manufacturing plants and design offices.
